body: Be sure to make the need to fork ASVS and start with level 1 items more prominent in the doc so beginners can get started with ASVS more easily.

Alright, here's what I have drafted so far. Let me know if it is a bit too much: 

I propose a change of title for this subsection from "As a Replacement for Off-the-self Secure Coding Checklists" to this: 
> `As a Specialized Secure Coding Checklist` 

as to reflect that we want ASVS to be a secure coding checklist, but through a fork which I later on described. 

Retaining this paragraph, but I am a bit confused with the second sentence, so probably needs more help and clarification what we mean by this part.  
`Many organizations can benefit from adopting the ASVS, by choosing one of the three levels, or by forking ASVS and changing what is required for each application risk level in a domain specific way. We encourage this type of forking as long as traceability is maintained, so that if an application has passed requirement 4.1, this means the same thing for forked copies as the standard as it evolves.`

Added this paragraph for more explanation about this ASVS usage and some guidelines for the forking process: 
`Ideally, every organization should have their own forked ASVS, select their requirements tailor-fitted for them and their applications. So if the organization is not using GraphQL, Websockets or SOAP web service on their applications, they should drop those sections from their forked ASVS. The forking process must start with looking at ASVS level 1 requirements as a baseline for the organization and then gradually move into ASVS level 2 or 3 as needed with based on their organization's risk level. Organizations must use their forked ASVS as a secure coding checklist for secure application development, preferably with guidance from security engineers or security architects alike. In this way, organizations will have a unified and clear secure coding checklist applicable for them and be used across all development teams. `

For the placement/arrangement in this page https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x04-Assessment_and_Certification.md, I kept reading through it and I noticed we have a subsection entitled "Testing Method", so I think it would be nice and practical to bundle this subsection with `As a Driver for Agile Application Security` and `As Detailed Security Architecture Guidance` and this `As a Replacement for Off-the-shelf Secure Coding Checklists or [with my new title up for discussion]`, then name all three of them in a subsection entitled "Secure Software Development". In this way, it stands out more compared to being just part of other uses for ASVS. I believe we want ASVS to be a guide for secure development as its main usage, so hopefully that brings it to a good point.

Is there an existing fork that can be used as a reference implementation, such as an ["_Off-the-shelf Secure Coding Checklists_"](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x04-Assessment_and_Certification.md#as-a-replacement-for-off-the-shelf-secure-coding-checklists) that we intend to replace?

This issue is simply a request to enhance our discussion of forking in the intro in 0x04-Assessmentxxx file.

The current text is the following and I'd like to expand on why forking ASVS is so important.

### As a Replacement for Off-the-shelf Secure Coding Checklists

Many organizations can benefit from adopting the ASVS, by choosing one of the three levels, or by forking ASVS and changing what is required for each application risk level in a domain-specific way. We encourage this type of forking as long as traceability is maintained so that if an app has passed requirement 4.1, this means the same thing for forked copies as the standard as it evolves.
I believe we should publish at least one example of a fork as the reference implementation.

> I believe we should publish at least one example of a fork as the reference implementation.

What would be the goal or the message for that?

We have abstract "this is the way to go" description which is short and clear enough and fits to document. But I think, it make sense to provide more clear instructions, how to do it and additionally arguments and benefits what forker can achieve.

For example, forking:
* take over latest release
* clean up (remove) categories which you don't need
* clean up (remove) requirements which you don't need
* add your own requirements, but use requirement numbers like:
   * V100, V101 for additional category
   * V2.100 for additional subcateogry for existing category
   * V2.2.100 for additional requirement for existing subcategory

Benefits:
* if to use steps above, it's easy to adopts minor releases (like v4.0 > v4.0.2)
* changes (added, modified, deleted requirements) in ASVS "bleeding edge" version are labeled, it's possible to take over new requirements to own forked version before new ASVS version is released.
Guys, did we have a way forward for this issue?
This is big concept issue and is a bit part of v5.0 goals. https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1127.
